title: Second pillar of Islam – Salah
intro: Salah is the second pillar of Islam: five prayers every day, at their set times.

learn.html: The second pillar of Islam – and the second main Islamic duty – is Salah (prayer).

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) tells us in the Qur’an to keep up the prayer, because prayer keeps a person away from shameful and evil deeds (Al-‘Ankabut, 29:45).
Salah is the most complete way of showing our obedience and thankfulness to Allah (SWT). It is commanded in the Qur’an, and the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) showed us how to pray.

learn.text: Five prayers in 24 hours, each at its own time

items.label: Dhuhr – When the sun has passed the middle of the sky.
Asr – Halfway between Dhuhr and sunset.
Maghrib – When the sun has set.
Isha – When the night has fully come.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember: three times when we must not pray
learn.html:
1. When the sun is rising. 2. When the sun is setting. 3. When the sun is in the middle of the sky.
That is about 45 minutes after sunrise, 45 minutes before sunset, and 5–10 minutes while the sun is at its highest.
With Salah we thank Allah for all the blessings He has given us in this world (dunya), and we hope for His mercy and reward in the next world (akhirah).
A Muslim knows that every prayer is a meeting with Allah (SWT), and that Salah reminds us of the Day of Judgement. Salah also protects us from doing wrong.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: “The first thing a person will be asked about on the Day of Judgement is the prayer. If the prayer is good, the rest of their deeds will be good; if it is bad, the rest of their deeds will be bad.” <small>(Tabarani)</small>
We build the habit of praying from early childhood, and Salah becomes a duty from the moment we come of age, for the rest of our life.

learn.title: 💬 Talk with your muallim
learn.html: Salah – the joy of my life.
